evidence.quoted_text: const addArgs = ['-C', repoRoot, 'worktree', 'add', '-B', reviewBranch, wtPath, expectedSha];
evidence.reason: Line 689 unconditionally uses `worktree add -B`, which force-resets an existing `reviewBranch` to `expectedSha`. The supplied code’s own safety contract (the add failure message at line 693) explicitly recognizes unpushed commits on a review branch and instructs callers to preserve them when an old worktree holds the branch, but there is no corresponding branch-ref check when `removePrWorktree` has left the branch with no worktree. In that case the next resolution sees no worktree candidate, falls through to line 689, and `-B` discards the only reference to the unpushed commit. That is an implementation defect in existing no-silent-destruction behavior, not a new protection requirement; the smallest fix is to inspect the existing branch before resetting and refuse or preserve a durable rescue ref when it contains commits not reachable from `expectedSha`.
